from decimal import Decimal

from reportlab.pdfbase import pdfmetrics
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

from ledgerline.billing import invoice_total
from ledgerline.models import Invoice, Line
from ledgerline.utils.money import format_currency


def wrap_text(text: str, width: int, font: str, size: int) -> list[str]:
    """Greedy word wrap using the font metrics."""
    words, lines, cur = text.split(), [], ""
    for w in words:
        trial = f"{cur} {w}".strip()
        if pdfmetrics.stringWidth(trial, font, size) <= width:
            cur = trial
        else:
            lines.append(cur)
            cur = w
    if cur:
        lines.append(cur)
    return lines


def draw_header(c: canvas.Canvas, invoice: Invoice, fonts: dict[str, str]) -> int:
    c.setFont(fonts["bold"], 20)
    c.drawString(40, 800, f"Invoice {invoice.number}")
    c.setFont(fonts["body"], 10)
    c.drawString(40, 782, invoice.customer.name)
    for i, line in enumerate(invoice.customer.address_lines):
        c.drawString(40, 768 - 12 * i, line)
    c.drawRightString(555, 800, invoice.issued.strftime("%d %b %Y"))
    return 720


def draw_lines(c: canvas.Canvas, lines: list[Line], y: int, fonts: dict[str, str]) -> int:
    c.setFont(fonts["body"], 10)
    for ln in lines:
        for i, part in enumerate(wrap_text(ln.description, 330, fonts["body"], 10)):
            c.drawString(40, y, part)
            if i == 0:
                c.drawRightString(555, y, format_currency(ln.total))
            y -= 13
        y -= 4
    return y


def draw_totals(c: canvas.Canvas, invoice: Invoice, y: int, fonts: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    c.setFont(fonts["bold"], 11)
    c.drawRightString(555, y, f"Total {format_currency(invoice_total(invoice))}")

import io

from reportlab.lib.pagesizes import A4
from reportlab.pdfgen import canvas

from ledgerline.invoice_pdf.fonts import load_fonts
from ledgerline.invoice_pdf.layout import draw_header, draw_lines, draw_totals
from ledgerline.models import Invoice


def render_invoice_pdf(invoice: Invoice) -> bytes:
    fonts = load_fonts()
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    c = canvas.Canvas(buf, pagesize=A4)
    y = draw_header(c, invoice, fonts)
    y = draw_lines(c, invoice.lines, y, fonts)
    draw_totals(c, invoice, y, fonts)
    c.showPage()
    c.save()
    return buf.getvalue()

content.text: The unmodified tree fails too: one failure this time, three on the first run. So it is not the refactor. It fails only with -n 4 and different tests each time, which points at the workers sharing a sqlite database. Let me look at the db fixture.

content.text: That is it. Every test that uses the store fixture opens the same file, tmp/test.db. With pytest-xdist (-n 4) four worker processes run at once, so they open and write that one file concurrently and sqlite answers 'database is locked'. A serial run, which is what make test does, never overlaps, so the problem only shows up in make ci and in CI, and only for whichever tests happen to overlap. The fix is to give each worker its own file, using the PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER environment variable that xdist sets to gw0, gw1 and so on.

# pytest-xdist runs one process per worker. PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER is gw0, gw1, ... and is unset in a serial run.
DB_PATH = Path(f"tmp/test-{os.environ.get('PYTEST_XDIST_WORKER', 'main')}.db")
